actual_item.title: Hecke Specht theory specialises to group Specht theory at q = 1
actual_item.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $q=1\in F$, and let $H_{F,1}(S_n)$ be the specialization of the generic type-A Hecke algebra at $v\mapsto1$, so that $H_{F,1}(S_n)\cong F[S_n]$ with $T_w\mapsto w$ ([[prop-group-algebra-and-finite-field-specializations-of-the-generic-hecke-algebra]]). Then the Hecke theory of this page specializes as follows.
1. The Murphy elements $m_\mu=\sum_{w\in S_\mu}T_w$ specialize to the row symmetrizers $\sum_{w\in S_\mu}w$, and the Murphy basis $\{m_{st}\}$ of $H_{F,1}(S_n)$ specializes to the Murphy basis of the group algebra $F[S_n]$ (the base change $\mathbb Z[S_n]\to F[S_n]$ of the integral Murphy basis).
2. For every $\lambda\vdash n$ the specialization of the page's Hecke Specht module $S^{\lambda}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) is the ordinary Specht module in the Dipper-James convention: $S^{\lambda}_{q=1}\cong S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ as $F[S_n]$-modules, with the standard polytabloid basis ([[thm-standard-polytabloid-basis]]); the specialized cell form is the standard bilinear form on $S^{\lambda}_k$ whose radical defines the James quotient $D^{\lambda}$ ([[def-modular-specht-form-and-radical-quotient]]).
3. The quantum characteristic of $q=1$ is $e=\operatorname{char}(F)$ when $\operatorname{char}(F)>0$, and $e=\infty$ when $\operatorname{char}(F)=0$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]); in characteristic $p>0$ a partition is $e$-regular exactly when it is $p$-regular. Hence $D^{\lambda}_{q=1}\ne0$ exactly for $p$-regular $\lambda$ ([[thm-simple-type-a-hecke-modules-are-indexed-by-e-regular-partitions]]), and for non-$p$-regular $\lambda$ one has $\mathrm{rad}\,S^{\lambda}=S^{\lambda}$, so not every Specht module remains simple in characteristic $p$. This matches the group-side classification [[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]] and the conjugate-sign dictionary [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]]. In characteristic $0$ the specialization is split semisimple and all Specht modules are irreducible.
actual_item.strategy: Base-change the Murphy cellular basis along $\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]\to F$, $v\mapsto1$: the structure constants are polynomials in $q$, so specialization gives a cellular basis of $F[S_n]$, and the cell modules specialize to the modules with the specialized triangular multiplication. The identification with the Dipper-James Specht module uses the printed p. 25 convention warning of the source together with the conjugate-sign duality of [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]]; the polytabloid/Murphy basis comparison is [[thm-standard-polytabloid-basis]]. The simple-label statement is the specialization of [[thm-simple-type-a-hecke-modules-are-indexed-by-e-regular-partitions]] at $e=\operatorname{char}(F)$, compared with [[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]]. The direction of information is one-way (this item imports the group classification and no group-side item depends on the Hecke theory). No choice is used.

references.title: Mathas, Iwahori-Hecke Algebras and Schur Algebras of the Symmetric Group, Chapter 1 sections 1-2 (specialization) and the p. 25 convention warning, printed pp. 3-6 and 25
Kleshchev, Symmetric groups and related Hecke algebras, Remark 5.5 and section 5.3 (the q=1, xi=1 case), p. 24

findings.false_use: Statement(3): zero labelled form quotient for a non-p-regular shape implies that not every Specht remains simple in characteristic p.
findings.countermodel: F=F_2,n=2,q=1,e=2: F_2[S_2]=F_2[u]/u^2. Ordinary Spechts (2),(1,1) are both one-dimensional trivial modules, hence simple. The column form is zero, but its actual module head is itself.

actual_item.title: The complete weight-one decomposition matrix for S3 at p=3
actual_item.statement: Take $e=p=3$ and the weight-one configuration $n=3$, $\gamma=\varnothing$ of [[thm-weight-one-block-decomposition-pattern]]; the three partitions of $3$ with $3$-core $\varnothing$ are $\lambda_1=(3)\rhd\lambda_2=(2,1)\rhd\lambda_3=(1,1,1)$ ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). The block of $S_3$ at $p=3$ therefore has the complete decomposition matrix, in the source's Weyl/simple normalisation and with rows and columns in the order $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3$, equal to $\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$; applying the Schur functor and the conjugation/duality dictionary gives the Murphy Specht rows $[S^{\lambda_1}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_2}_{\mathrm M}]$, $[S^{\lambda_2}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_2}_{\mathrm M}]+[D^{\lambda_3}_{\mathrm M}]$, $[S^{\lambda_3}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_3}_{\mathrm M}]$, which in the page's $3$-regular labels $(3),(2,1)$ is the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ with rows $(3),(2,1),(1,1,1)$ ([[thm-nakayama-block-classification-for-symmetric-groups]], [[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]]); the group-side entries are verified directly from the two-dimensional model $S^{(2,1)}$ of characteristic $3$, whose all-ones vector spans a trivial submodule with sign quotient, together with $S^{(3)}=\operatorname{triv}$ and $S^{(1,1,1)}=\operatorname{sgn}$.
actual_item.strategy: List the partitions of $3$ with $3$-core $\varnothing$: $(3)$ and $(1,1,1)$ remove their unique $3$-hook and $(2,1)$ has no $3$-hook, giving exactly the three labels in the stated dominance order. Apply the weight-one theorem to obtain the bidiagonal Weyl matrix, then the Schur functor and the conjugation/duality dictionary $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}=(S^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^{*}$, $D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}=(D^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^{*}$ to pass from the Murphy rows to the group-side matrix with rows and columns in the $p$-regular labels $(3),(2,1)$, and finally compare with the direct computation from the standard module: in characteristic $3$ the all-ones vector of $S^{(2,1)}$ spans a trivial submodule with sign quotient, so the rows of $S^{(3)},S^{(2,1)},S^{(1,1,1)}$ are $(1,0),(1,1),(0,1)$ in the labels $(3),(2,1)$, and the simple labels are those of [[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]]. The two computations agree entry by entry, which is the verification of the example. No choice principle is used. Sources: Mathas, Proposition 5.38 and the accompanying discussion of $q=1$ (printed pp. 61-63); the published $S_3$ matrix.

findings.false_use: Strategy explicitly asserts S_DJ^lambda=(S_M^{lambda′})^* and similarly D, omitting theta.
findings.countermodel: F=F_3,n=3,q=1,lambda=(3): ordinary S^(3) is trivial; S_M^(111) is sign, and its contragredient dual is sign, not trivial. The correct actual NEW50 comparison requires sign theta. The stated group-side numeric matrix can still be obtained intrinsically, but this module identity is false.
